African Playhouse

Board, card and dice games from African traditions, such as Songo, Oware and Fanorona, played against the computer, on one device or at a private online table.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Songo, Oware, Fanorona and Morabaraba are played across Africa, yet they are hard to find in a careful digital form. Their rules change from one region and one source to another. Relatives who live in different countries have few simple ways to sit at the same table.

02

What it does

Thirteen playable games: eight classics (Ludo Afrique, Yatzy Afrique, Dames d'Afrique, Snakes & Ladders Afrique, Tic-Tac-Toe Afrique, Water Sort Afrique, African Match Garden and African Empires, a solo campaign set in a fictional Mali of 1325) and five traditional games (Songo, Oware, Naija Shapes, Fanorona and Morabaraba). Four of them follow a named edition: Nkul Beti for Songo, Abapa for Oware, Fanoron-Tsivy for Fanorona and twelve-cattle Morabaraba. Most games offer computer opponents, local play on one device and private online tables. Eleven more traditions, from Bao to Diketo, are listed with their region and planned rules. The atelier sells decorative boards, dice and tokens that never change the rules or the odds.

03

How it is built

React, with Supabase for guest sessions, accounts and the real-time private tables, hosted on Netlify. Solo and local games need no account and are saved on the device. An online table uses a guest session with no email. The whole site is in English and French, with a dark and a light theme, high contrast, larger text and reduced motion. Payments run in test mode only on this version.
